utterances.text: Why did you not want to go in their car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a moment that I didn't feel safe for myself and for the others. So in these circumstances, I felt better to drive in my own car, even though Haradinaj and Balaj insisted for us to come with them. So I kept insisting on my own. They kept asking us to go with them. I mean that I was afraid to go in their car. I felt more secure to travel in my car myself and my friends -- for my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you show them the travel document you had received from the KLA village commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did show them the document I had obtained from the village commander, Mr. Maxhun Cekaj, but Daut tore it up and invited that person to come to the place where we were. He came there. Daut started to shout to him, telling him, "Why have you provided them with this piece of paper to these FARK soldiers. They have no place here. They should leave Kosova. We will fight against them," and things like this. So he threatened Maxhun Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Balaj saying anything during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very bad moment. Mr. Balaj brought out his pistol and fired several times, five or six times maybe, and he did that to strike fear among us, to force us to follow him, to do what he had planned to do with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where did he fire these five or six shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very close to us, in my presence, in the presence of Maxhun Cekaj, and all the others. He was -- we were two or three metres apart from one other in the middle of the village, to cut it short, but he didn't fire in our direction, but in the air because he wanted to scare us and to order us to get into their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point, did you go to Gllogjan that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly, after all we went. Mr. Daut Haradinaj left first; Idriz Balaj after him; we were in the middle and we left to -- for Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So you went in three vehicles, Witness 29. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get from Irzniq to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very certain to give you minutes, but it's very close from the place we were. I would say that the distance between the last village -- the last house of one village and the first of the other village might be two kilometres. It takes you five or ten minutes driving. It depends on how fast you drive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, this last question and the details we received there, where the Chamber knows that it's two kilometres, does not assist in any way to better understand the testimony. Of course, we have seen the statement so, of course, if something would have happened on the way that might be useful to ask about it. But isn't that totally superfluous?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's a point well taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where did you go when you got to Gllogjan, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Gllogjan, we were told to go to the staff of Mr. Ramush Haradinaj. Once we arrived in front of the staff, Daut Haradinaj parked his car in front of our car. We parked behind him. And we were about 50 metres away from the entrance to the staff. Idriz Balaj parked behind us. I mean that all the time we were in between two cars. I got out of the car. I left my colleagues in the car. I left my weapon there, Kalashnikov, and walked in the direction of the staff of Mr. Ramush Haradinaj to meet him. In the meantime, I don't know what Daut was doing, but as I said he parked his car in front of us and we were obliged to stop. There was nothing else we could do. There was a large number of soldiers surrounding us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there surrounding you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an accurate number, but there was a large number. It was impossible for me to count them, and it didn't enter my mind to count them, actually. If I can go on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if the witness could tell us an approximate number. I do understand you did not count them. Would you say there were ten? 50? 200?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village, there was a number of soldiers; but in the staff of Mr. Ramush Haradinaj, I saw that he was talking to a number of about 40, 50 soldiers lined up in two columns. And from what I understood, he was addressing them as their commander. When he saw me walking towards him, he told the soldiers, "Wait a little because a friend of mine, my best friend, had come," and he came towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These 40 to 50 soldiers that Ramush was addressing, were they uniformed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those who were there, they were uniformed. They were lined, as I said, in two columns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At that time, did you have a conversation with Mr. Haradinaj, this is Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had a conversation. It was a very friendly, fraternal conversation. I told him, "I came here because Daut Haradinaj and Togeri came to Irzniq village to force us to come here to you." I showed to him that I refused to travel in their car, and then I told him where I was going and why I had gone there. And in the end Mr. Ramush Haradinaj said to me that, "You and your soldiers," the soldiers who were with me, I mean, "don't need to have any piece of paper. Nobody will prevent you. You may be with three or 300 other soldiers. You are free to go wherever you wish. Nobody can prevent you." And I took it as a normal occurrence, of course, as things should be. In fact, I expected this of him. We shook hands and I left. He said, "You are free to go now."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you begin to walk back to the car at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, the place where I had parked the car and the place where I entered Mr. Haradinaj's staff, it was a distance of 20 metres. I was walking on the direction of the car to continue our trip to Pacaj village. In the meantime, Daut and Togeri came, and Idriz Balaj came, and there was an exchange on the way. They went to Mr. Ramush Haradinaj and talked with him. I don't know what they talked about. And then Mr. Ramush Haradinaj changed his mind and told me, "Take those" - by "those" I mean the soldiers who were with me - "and go back to where you came from because there is a problem which might last -- before it's resolved, a couple of days might pass day." He didn't specify how many days they needed for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When Ramush Haradinaj said those words to you: "Take those soldiers and go back to where you came from," what tone of voice was that said in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now things deteriorated. It was no longer the friendly tone we used or he used before. It was now harsher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Tell us what happened then, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I walked in the direction of the car and told Idriz to get into the car because we have to turn back to Irzniq village, because the KLA under Ramush's command doesn't let us to go this way. We have to go back. Idriz seemed perplexed because he didn't expect what happened. He said, "Why? For what reason?" I said, "Come into the car because I have to go back." Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. Tell us what happened then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meantime, I was walking towards my car. Idriz wanted to get into the car. Mr. Haradinaj -- both Haradinaj brothers and Balaj were following behind me two, three metres away. And at the moment Mr. Haradinaj said, "Get those and get lost." I said to Idriz, "Get into the car." And then at that moment, Mr. Haradinaj came on my right side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can we hear that once more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, if I can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The Trial Chambers would like you to clarify your last answer which was: "At that moment Mr. Haradinaj said, "Get those and" something. We didn't understand what you said, Witness 29, could you repeat that last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Including the answer, please, who said it, Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer your question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, Witness 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I wonder with the Trial Chamber's permission from here on out since there are two Haradinajs involved, Ramush and Daut.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Instead of saying "Mr. Haradinaj," can you please use the first name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Can I continue now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj used this expression: "Get lost." What can I say? "Go away. I don't want to lay eyes on you anymore." And he was following behind me. And at the point he came on my right side, and I saw him with his pistol in his right-hand. Idriz was leaning on the side of -- on the front door of the car, and he was about to enter the car. At that moment, Ramush Haradinaj overtook me on my right side and went to Idriz Ukehaxhaj. He had the pistol on his right hand, and on his left hand was made like a fist. He had the pistol on the right and the fisted left hand, and then he hit Idriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: May I stop you there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Members of the Trial Chamber, the witness just made a motion with his hands describing what he saw Ramush Haradinaj do to Idriz Ukehaxhaj. And I would invite the members of the Trial Chamber, does the Trial Chamber want me to describe that for the record? Does the Trial Chamber want to do it themselves?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The witness - and I invite Defence to correct me if I'm wrong - the witness held both hands out in front of him with clenched fists, and he moved his hands together in a partial clapping motion, I would characterise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shoulder high, approximately. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did -- with that motion, Witness 29, did Ramush Haradinaj actually hit Idriz Ukehaxhaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj hit him on both sides of his face. On his right hand was the pistol. His left hand was clenched into a fist, and he hit him on both sides of his face. And his face was covered in blood, I mean Idriz Ukehaxhaj's face.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us the degree of force that you saw Ramush Haradinaj use during the -- during that blow, please, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I can't tell you the degree of force, but I can tell you that it was a strong blow. You see, his face was covered in flood. So it was quite a powerful hit, such a hit that covered his face in blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what had Idriz been doing at the time he was hit? Was he -- what was he doing when he was -- he received this blow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. He was doing nothing. Please, what could he do? He wasn't expecting that. I was very close to him, but I couldn't intervene because everything happened in a very short time. Nobody was expecting it. We never thought that such a thing would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After that first blow was struck by Ramush, did he continue to administer more blows? Did the attack continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first blow and, yes, it continued. At the same time, Mr. Daut Haradinaj, Ramush's brother, and Balaj attacked the other soldiers, Petrit and Azem, two soldiers, because Idriz was under Ramush at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please describe the attack for us, if you could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a very difficult moment for me to describe a hundred per cent. I'll try my best. At that time, the car was parked close to a wall, and Idriz was attacked by Ramush on both sides of his face, while Azem and Petrit were behind the car, close to the wall. At that moment, Daut Haradinaj and Idriz Balaj attacked Petrit and Azem. Everything happened in a couple of moments. They were attacked physically, not in words, but they were beaten. They started hitting them with pistols, punching them, and then there were other soldiers that participated in the beating. It was a very ugly beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What were the numbers of the KLA soldiers that were involved in the beating? There was four of you, four FARK members. How many KLA were there involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number took part, but not all the soldiers that were in Gllogjan. I could say maybe 20 or 30 took part in the beating. It was a very powerful beating, but there were other soldiers who were there present but seemed not to like what was happening, but they couldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you beaten yourself during this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was beaten as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please describe that for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. I was attacked from behind by Mr. Daut Haradinaj and Mr. Balaj. The first time I received the blow, this was a blow on my head with a gun, a pistol I think; and after that, other blows came, all sorts of blows, punches with the butts of the guns, the Kalashnikovs. They used them as sticks to beat us. And all kinds of other beatings on the body, on the head. There was no part of our body that was not hit; both me and the other three soldiers that were beaten at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were there any words spoken to you during this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the moment they started to beat us, they also were saying things. Among the words that they said were, "We will kill you. We will eliminate you, not only you but your commanders Sali Ceku and Tahir Zemaj." They were offending us, calling us names, all kind of swear words, our mothers and everything. And one of them said, "Wait, we'll kill (redacted)." And at a certain moment, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj said, "No, I'll kill him with my own hand," and he jumped on me from behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is Ramush who jumped on you from behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first time it was Toger and Daut, his brother, Ramush's brother; while the second time when these words were spoken, "Let's kill (redacted)," Mr. Ramush Haradinaj said, "I'll kill him with my own hand," and he jumped on me from behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After Ramush jumped on you from behind, what did he do to you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Ramush Haradinaj jumped on me from behind. There was a moment when he had the pistol in his hand and wanted to kill me, and I was in is certain position. I wasn't lying down, but I also wasn't standing. I was trying to protect myself from him, from Mr. Haradinaj, and suddenly I heard a gun-shot. I didn't understand at the time that the bullet had hit me because I was receiving other blows and my whole body was aching and was in pain. So I didn't understand that I was hit, but there was a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to stop you there for a moment, if I may. You said just a moment ago, this is at line 12: "At that time, Ramush Haradinaj jumped on me from behind. There was a moment when he had the pistol in his hand, and he wanted to kill me." Please describe that for us, you said: "There was a moment when he had the pistol in his hand, and he wanted to kill me." What was he doing with the pistol that makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj. Everything was clear. Mr. Haradinaj said himself that, "I will kill (redacted) with my own hand," and he came to me and I don't know what else to explain, how much more clearly to explain, because he wanted to kill me. He jumped on me. Maybe he had planned this. I don't know what else to say. He jumped on me with a pistol against my shoulder or my neck, and I was trying to protect myself as best I could, and then I heard the gun-shot. I was hit on the right arm. The bullet entered the arm here and then came out ten or 12 centimetres lower in the arm. I was trying, as I said, to protect myself, not to allow him to do that; but still, a bullet hit me and fortunately I did not die.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I have to ask you this for the record. Who fired the bullet that hit you in the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Put in that form, given the witness's evidence thus far and indeed what is in the contents of his witness statement, that is not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say from whose weapon?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. The witness's evidence at the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and indeed his witness statement does not permit a answer to that question in terms. What Mr. Kearney can properly do is elicit the factual circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Which is exactly what I'm trying to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Perhaps the witness might just remove his earphones for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My intent --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just explain the objection before Mr. Kearney responds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The witness statement makes it clear on its face that the witness did not see which gun the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He draws certain inferences in his witness statement, and in particular paragraph 7 on, I think, page 4, as to how that might have occurred -- sorry, paragraph 7 on page 11, where he describe there being a lot of weapons fired around him but drawing certain inferences to the location of Mr. Haradinaj in respect of this incident. And he expresses an opinion based on that. But it is in my submission extremely important- and he's repeated that many his evidence- than to rather to ask him a question who shot you, when on the face of it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the point is clear. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, my intent was -- and, Your Honour, I am operating under a very severe time-frame here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And my intent was to ask him this question and ask him why he says that. I'm very aware what was in the statement, and I'm aware that Mr. Emmerson has a long time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With respect, that is, in its present form, nothing more than an opinion. What Mr. Kearney can properly do is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we do not know yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm in Your Honours' hands, of course. I don't want to take time on an objection. But, with respect, the way the evidence emerges both in writing and orally is that the witness saw, heard, and felt certain things; and from those things, he drew conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you are aware of the problems Mr. Emmerson. Could you please rephrase your question. Keep in mind the concerns of Mr. Emmerson, and then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, how was Ramush holding the gun in relation to your body when you felt yourself being shot?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness does not have his earphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for assisting us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, how was Ramush holding the gun in relation to your body immediately before you felt yourself being shot in the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I was not lying down, but I was not standing. Can I demonstrate, please? I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: With the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. And be aware that we'll have to describe that for the record what you are showing us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of my knees was almost on the ground, and I was trying to defend myself, leaning -- most of my body was leaning this way. I can't explain it properly. I was trying to protect myself. He had his pistol here on my shoulder; and during the movement, I heard the shot and the bullet came through the arm. The position -- it was a very difficult position I was in. I couldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness moved in a way where he was kneeling down with a twisted body, looking upwards with his body close to the ground. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And may I ask: The pistol was on your shoulder you said. Would that mean it was at close range or touching the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pistol was against my neck at the moment that he was saying, "I'll kill him with my own hand." And because I was moving, he could not hit me on my neck and the bullet hit my arm and not on the neck where he wanted to hit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So you're describing the bullet hit you on your right arm, close to the shoulder. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you're saying "he," this is -- when you said: "He could not hit me on my neck," you're referring to Ramush. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to Ramush, exactly. He wanted to hit me on my neck; but because of the movement that I was doing at the time, the bullet did not hit me in my neck but on my right arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, how long did this beating last, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how long. It started suddenly. It ended suddenly, when they were satisfied. So both the starting moment and the ending moment were sudden. At that time, I saw they were dragging the other soldiers by their hair. Daut Haradinaj and Idriz Balaj were dragging them by their hair and beating them at the same time. They were dragging them towards the village Gllogjan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, could I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- towards the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- ask one question. Was the shot you heard when you were hit any different from what you heard when others have used their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that the other shots were stronger. At the time, when I heard this particular shot, I don't know whether my ears were blocked or something, but I did not hear the same kind of sound as the other sounds. I cannot explain it to you. Everything was so sudden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You said that the attack stopped suddenly. Please tell us what happened when it stopped. Was anything said to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the attack stopped, I saw Idriz, Petrit, and Azem being dragged by their hair, by Daut and Balaj, and they were being beaten with Kalashnikovs and with the butts of the pistols, also punching and so on. They were dragging them towards the headquarters. At that time, Ramush still had his pistol in his hand. He kept that in his hand all the time, and he said to me, "You only got two minutes to leave the village of Gllogjan. And walk straight, straight ahead on the main road. You've got only two minutes to leave the village," while the other soldiers were taken into the headquarters of the Gllogjan village, Mr. Haradinaj's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then did you then leave Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I left the -- the place where the event happened. We were surrounded by soldiers at the time. I was allowed to leave. I was walking; and about 150 metres away from that place, I took a turn and walked through the village, which was kind of a yard. I was hiding there, close to a wall. It was the yard of a house. I did not see any people living there, so I don't know whether that place was lived in or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were told to walk away on the main road. Why did you not do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not do that because if I had followed the main road, Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Ramush Haradinaj, did not need to tell me, Go and follow the main road. He could have just told me, Leave, go. So I thought maybe he would kill me himself or order some of his subordinates to kill me. That's why as soon as I left the place where all this happened, I tried to avoid that risk. That's why I left and turned left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you eventually make it back to the FARK command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after some time. I don't know how long I stayed there. I walked about two kilometres to my village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, from the question, you could learn that Mr. Kearney might not be interested in all the details in how you got back. So you got back to the FARK command. Next question would be, Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you got back to the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- FARK command, did you receive medical treatment for your injuries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence, on medical treatment and follow-up, is there any problem with leading in that respect? Then, Mr. Kearney, you could take the witness through the medical department and leading him. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have no objection to Mr. Kearney leading with those issues, but I think there is no independent medical evidence available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Of course, instead of asking all these questions to him, but rather to take him through his statement. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the one exhibit I do want to use during this testimony is a photograph. It is 65 ter 1311. I'd like it shown, if I may, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And at the same time, if you want to hear any details by the medical treatment, you can do that by leading, since the Defence, and I see the other Defence joining, have no objections to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number for the next document would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P264, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Any objection against admission if it would be asked? Not. Then if you tender it, Mr. Kearney, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, do you recognise the arm depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my arm, and this is the wound I received from Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The bullet that you were shot with, did it -- please tell us where it entered your body and where it exited your body and show us -- tell us what we are viewing here in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The bullet entered the upper part of the arm and exited here. The larger hole that you can see here is the exit point. The smaller hole is the entry point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Members of the Trial Chamber, we have two other photographs here. Does the Trial Chambers want me to go into those, or should I move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what's on the photographs; but if it is similar, then I don't think there's any dispute about that there may be an entrance and an exit bullet-hole on the arm of this witness because that's what the photo shows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask to be clear about these two holes. I see one, this is unambiguous, which is, well, in the middle of the upper rather. It seems to be rather to the front side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that's a point well taken. We do have another photograph I think shows the entry and the shoulder and the exit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, I would like to see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, it's common knowledge that the entry holes usually are the smaller ones and the exit holes are the bigger ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Just to show the exact location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please show the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do we show --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I think we need your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 840 -- I'm sorry. It's 311 -- 1311, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, do you recognise the photograph being shown now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same photograph, but there is a ruler here showing the distance between the two. At 0, you can see the entry point; and at approximately 10 centimetres, the exit point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber's sufficiently informed about the wounds, Mr. Kearney. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And beyond just the bullet wound in your arm, describe very briefly for us, please, your other injuries.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not have other wounds because I was not hit by other bullets. Those were just the results of beatings, then I recovered from those bruises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you ever see your three colleagues again after you left Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, would be leading in as far as "the others" is concerned, would that find any objection or Mr. Guy-Smith or Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Within reason, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, I would like to ask you again, did you ever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, shall we ask him: Did you see the others that were with you in hospital later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them about three hours later. I can't be very precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us in general terms what their condition was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in an extremely bad state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what made them to be in a bad state, without too much details.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were badly beaten. Their heads were bandaged. They didn't feel well. They felt very weak. They could hardly stand. Azem Gashi had received a bullet injury also. It was a very, very bad situation. They had great pains. Their heads was covered in bandages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Gashi tell you how it was he came to be shot in the foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only that he had a bullet wound in his right leg, if I'm not mistaken. But the entire situation was very bad. We didn't know what to say to each other. Each of us started to recount what had happened to him, how they had experienced it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did your colleagues tell you what had happened to them after they were dragged off by the hair towards the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They were beaten also inside, then they were brought outside. They had been -- all their clothes had been taken off. They were left only in their underwear, and all the time being beaten; then they were ordered to run from Gllogjan village in the direction of Irzniq until to Kodrali, in front of the car. While they were firing their weapons in the ground, while they were ordered to run, they were firing left and right to force them to run under these circumstances, even though they were badly beaten and weak and could hardly walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did they tell you who it was that were firing their weapons at them at this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me that from Gllogjan to Kodrali, Daut Haradinaj and Idriz Balaj were firing their weapons. This is what they told me. And they also said that when they arrived in Irzniq village, there was a command called the Black Eagles under Idriz Balaj's command, and they were beaten there, too. They kept firing, and they kept running to Kodrali almost all the time until almost naked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I now, Witness 29, want to move on to my last area of conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to, with the Trial Chamber's permission, advance to the 10th of July, a few days later, to the village of Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you if in that village on that date you saw Ramush Haradinaj again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him again on the 10th. Mr. Ramush Haradinaj, accompanied by Rrustem Teta and Idriz Balaj and a group of about 30 men, all soldiers - I'm not sure about the exact number - came to our command in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These soldiers, what unit were they, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in black uniforms. They were called special unit or black uniforms. They had two names, I think: Black Eagles and Special Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you how specifically Ramush Haradinaj and Idriz Balaj were dressed on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were dressed in black uniforms, like the others, and they lined the soldiers in front of our command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what happened when these soldiers came to your command post on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came and lined the soldiers in front of -- lined up the soldiers in front of the building, and then they invited Tahir Zemaj and Sali Ceku, telling them to flee from Prapaqan in 30 minutes. They had only -- they were given only 30 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, did you hear this yourself, Witness 29?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did either Mr. Ceku or Mr. Zemaj respond when they were told by Ramush that they had 30 minutes to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both asked him, "Why?" Because it was an ultimatum to leave the place in 30 minutes. They were taken by surprise and asked why they had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did Ramush respond when they asked him why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- at that moment, Ramush raised his automatic rifle up and fired in the air, and he said, "Five minutes have passed, so you have only 25 minutes left," after firing several times in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point after that, did those men or did one or both of those men leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this incident, one evening, not many more days after the -- the few days, Sali Ceku came and I was sleeping, and he said to me, "Wake up. We have to leave Kosova, all of us, because they will kill all of us."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you then leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got up, prepared ourselves, talked with Commander Zemaj, and he said, "We must leave tonight." And he gave us another instruction: "If the situation doesn't change, I too will leave, because we haven't come here to kill each other."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember what date it was that you finally left Kosovo, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, I may make mistakes regarding the dates, but I think it was around the 17th. I think it is -- actually, I think it was 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That was 17th of July, 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 17th of July, 1998. It was 11.00, 12.00, around midnight when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Members of the Trial Chamber, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kearney. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am. And I want to if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With Your Honour's permission, I want to ask one or two questions at the outset about the notes issue and move on to the substance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, you told us yesterday that during 1998 you made a series of personal notes on separate sheets of paper about incidents that happened to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had to keep notes of -- note of everything, but I reported it to the commander, to show him also the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you also told us yesterday that when you compiled the blue notebook that you brought with you to court, you had those notes in your possession and copied notes directly into the notebook. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must be clear about one thing. Some of the notes that we kept at that time, we submitted to the command. Sometimes the commanders took them in the form we gave them; but when it had to do with some problems affecting me or whatever I did, one copy I handed to the commanders -- I showed it to the commander or kept the copy with me. So sometimes we gave them the notes, and sometimes we kept the notes -- I kept the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But, Witness 29, when you compiled the blue notebook you brought with you to court, you told us yesterday that you compiled that from notes that were still in your possession at the time you copied those notes into the notebook. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any reason to keep notes about anything other than real events, so the dates correspond to the events, just being transferred from one paper to another. This is what I brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please listen carefully to the question and please answer it. Is it correct that the entries in the blue notebook are all entries that you copied from individual pieces of paper that you recorded at the time of the events they describe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't keep track of all cases and everything. I just tried to keep record of the dates, because sometimes I don't need to keep -- to describe the events in writing because I remembered them very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, the question is whether what you wrote down in that notebook is just a copy of the text you find on these pieces of paper where you made your notes, whether you added anything, whether it's the same, whether it's less. Is it the same? You are nodding. Could you please respond, for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing is added, sir. Nothing is missing. Everything was copied as it actually was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that happened -- that process happened sometime in the last six weeks, Witness 29. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This process started and developed gradually. Even yesterday, I said it lasted for about one month and a half. It started after the date I gave some notes to the gentleman and some copies of the notes, then gradually I started to copy them from these pieces of paper to the notebook. But I cannot tell you it's one week, two weeks, one month, three months. But after the event I gave them, the representatives of the office, some copies of these notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Listen carefully. You told us yesterday you'd had the notebook for only one and a half months, that is, six weeks. So it must follow, mustn't it, that you copied the notes into the notebook sometime over the last six weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "approximately." I didn't say the exact date. I always say "approximately." By this I mean it may be six, seven, eight weeks. I cannot be precise. Were I certain, I would have told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's fine. Sometime in the last eight weeks let's say. So it must follow, you had all those original pieces of paper in your possession within the last eight weeks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the overwhelming majority of them, yes, of all the events. But, of course, I copied everything because I couldn't copy something without having the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how many of those notes have you since destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how many, but one of them may be still with me. Some I have discarded, and some are still with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you destroy most of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I may have destroyed something unintentionally, because I didn't think at that moment that it might be of use to me. And I thought that since I copied it in the notebook from the original, maybe I don't need it anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, the question was what percentage, more or less. So not whether you did it intentionally, but was it four out of five or was it just two out of five that you destroyed. I mean, proportions. Did you destroy most of them or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's say if I had ten, I have destroyed three or four; however, most of them are still there today -- even today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking always approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've been requested to provide those notes to the Prosecution I think on three separate occasions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let me put it to you specifically. On the 28th of August, last year, the Prosecution contacted you and asked you whether you were prepared to supply notes to the Defence and you said that you were not; and then again in early September, the Prosecution asked you if you were prepared to provide your original notes to them, and you refused to provide them to the Prosecution and said you didn't want to meet to discuss the matter with the Prosecution at that time; and then in December of last year, you provided certain notes, which are different from the notes in your notebook; and then in January, the Prosecution contacted you again and asked you to look for any other notes and provide the original notes to the Prosecution. That is the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you answer that question. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this question is severely compound. I don't know how -- I would ask that it be broken up. This witness is being asked to comment on four separate subject matters in one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, perhaps you briefly take the witness end-of-August request to provide them to the Defence and seek an answer to that. Is that correct, that you were asked to provide the notes to the Defence in August last year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the dates exactly because time is passing by; however, I do remember that several times I was asked to give these notes or personal notes, but I refused because I didn't want to put myself in -- at risk from Mr. Haradinaj, because I was certain that everything I would give them, his Defence would be notified, and I wouldn't feel secure and safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it is true that once you refused to give the notes to the Defence, then you were asked to give the notes to the Prosecution. You refused that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some representatives of the Tribunal - I don't know if they were Prosecutors or Defence lawyers - but several times I refused to give them the notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then, finally, in January of this year, you were specifically asked to make sure that you looked for all notes and brought the originals to the Tribunal, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these questions aim at one question. I think I gave a clear answer. I told you: I promise that I will bring them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, please respond to the question. What the aim of the questions is not a question is whether you had would then -- let me just look at the question again: "You were specifically asked then to make sure that you looked for all notes and brought the originals to the Tribunal," whether that was asked in January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not certain about the time. I think it was -- maybe it was in January. I promise to give them, the notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you then destroy the originals after promising to bring them, of any of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe that misstates his testimony. He is implying that the instruction happened after the January meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it is clear that it did, and I'll lay the foundation for it, because the witness says he copied them into his notebook within the last eight weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Objection overruled. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you explain why in those circumstances you chose to destroy some of the notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said, some I have destroyed, but the overwhelming part of them are still there. So it is still possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, the question simply is: You were invited to look for all of the notes and to bring them. Later on you started copying them, and you destroyed part of them. The question is: Why did you destroy them where it must have been clear to you that the originals were to be taken to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already told you. I didn't intend to destroy them. It was unintentional. I didn't know you needed these scraps of paper, these pieces of paper. Of course, it would have been easier for me to bring all those pieces of paper than to sit down and copy them in a notebook. For me, what mattered were the dates, the accurate dates of events. How can I say? I didn't think that it was more important to keep a piece of paper than a whole notebook; however, as I said, most of them do exist, even now. But I never -- it never occurred to me that it was necessary to bring them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, on the first page of the notebook that you've produced, you refer to various incidents that took place on the 3rd and the 5th of June of 1998, and you list the names of people. And when referring to yourself, you refer to yourself in the third person; in other words, you put your whole name down (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I do apologise. We'll redact the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You put your full name down in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's been redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Witness 29, if these are notes that you were making for your own recollection at the time, why would you write your own name in full in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes it's only my signature; sometimes it's my name, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's turn into private session in order to avoid further risks, and a further redaction will be made.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, I want to now move now to the events you've described on the 4th of July, just to explain the direction of the questions I'm going to ask you. I'm going to ask you, first of all, some questions about that particular incident that you've described, and then I'm going to ask you some more questions about FARK generally and about the description you've given of the problems that existed between the FARK and the KLA under Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, we are close at where we usually have a break, if you have a few short introductory questions, that's fine; if not, not to interrupt the 4th of July events.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have the break now and we'll resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, Mr. Kearney, if we would get the consent of the interpreters and the technicians, as far as courtrooms are concerned, we could continue until quarter past 2.00, but of course I'm in their hands. The urgency, of course, is that tomorrow is a non-hearing day. We'll then not sit for next week, and that's so if we could have the consent of the technicians and interpreters, I got the consent of two Trial Chambers, which would need a late start this afternoon. I see nodding yes. It makes me very happy. Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour very much as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I take it that if -- Mr. Kearney, do you expect -- well, of course I'm not going to ask you whether there will be many questions in re-examination, but at least there should be some time left for re-examination as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start now without further delay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, I'm going to suggest to you that the account that you have given to the Trial Chamber about the incident that occurred on the 4th of July contains a number of quite deliberate lies on your part. And there are two aspects of your account in particular that I want to explore with you briefly. First of all, the question of motive. If I've understood it correctly, you're saying that Ramush Haradinaj attacked your colleague Idriz Ukehaxhaj for no reason at all, in an entirely unprovoked attack. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Your evidence is that Ramush Haradinaj attacked your colleague Idriz Ukehaxhaj for no reason at all in an entirely unprovoked attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was a man you'd known when you were younger. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Mr. Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, we knew each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You'd known him when you were younger, and you had seen him in the first half of 1998 when you'd come in to discuss soldiers who would join in the conflict in Kosovo. He had been very pleased to welcome you at that point. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a very friendly meeting at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the commander of Irzniq, you've told us, was a man called Maxhun Cekaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. Now he's dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for just one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you were wearing a uniform, is that right, on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which occasion are you talking about? Could you speak more concretely?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the 4th of July, when you were in Gllogjan, you had picked up a uniform, you told us I think, from Irzniq. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were the other three men with you wearing uniforms as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had uniforms. I had a uniform. We all had uniforms of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there a patch on the arm of that uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the soldiers at that time, both in Prapaqan and soldiers of Mr. Haradinaj, did not have patches. But we were part of the army; both Mr. Haradinaj's part and the part that was under Tahir Zemaj's control. Some of them did have patches, but some soldiers did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the four of you, did you have patches with insignia on your arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. I'm not sure about them, but I don't believe they had patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the other soldiers of the army that you were with, what were the patches on their arms -- what did they say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same patches as Mr. Haradinaj's soldiers had. We did not have different patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You had UCK patches on your arms, generally, didn't you, in that group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Almost all had the patches of the KLA, but some of the FARK were also members of the KLA. They were all together. There was nothing wrong with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There was a very close relationship between them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a close relationship and we expected for that to go on, and we never expected what happened with Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come to what happened, generally, with your entry into Kosovo in a little while. But just so that the Judges understand, there was no separate FARK uniform. FARK soldiers wore KLA uniforms and badges generally. You'll agree with that, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. The uniforms changed because -- were different because they came from different parts of the world; however, most of the soldiers, both those under the command of Mr. Haradinaj and those under the command of Tahir Zemaj, used the same badge. They were all part of the same force.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were all part of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this time. I wonder if my colleague could specify what time he's referring to during these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you came into Kosovo on the 24th of June, the soldiers that came with you, any of them that wore patches wore KLA patches, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we entered Kosovo, we entered with the flag of our brigade; and on the flag, there was the emblem of the KLA. There was an eagle in the middle of the flag, and there were two hands; one saying "F," which is the letter F, which was the FARK, and the other one, the other part of the army. We were a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, those soldiers that had patches and insignia on their arms and on their caps had the UCK insignia, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some who had those patches, but not all. For example, I did not have that patch myself, but that did not stop me for being part of -- from being part of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please carefully listen to the question, because Mr. Emmerson now two, three, or four times asked you whether patches were worn by your soldiers, if they wore any patches, if these were KLA patches. Is my understanding that that was the case correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to answer the question. I said that there were some who had the KLA patches because the senior representatives of the army had agreed upon that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "Why" is a different question. "Whether they all had" is also a different question. But those who were wearing patches were wearing KLA patches. That's well understood now I think. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you'd had a very helpful meeting with Mr. Haradinaj in the early part of 1998. You say you saw him on the 4th of July in Irzniq, and he was very pleasant to you, is that correct? He greeted you as a friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you claim you went inside the headquarters, and he greeted you as a friend there, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then suddenly, for no reason, he attacked your colleague. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the account you've given of this incident is not true. Let me move on to another respect, and then I'll put to you specifically what I suggest is the truth about this incident. Could you be provided with the yellow file, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours have the yellow file. I'm dealing with it this way simply for speed. Can I indicate that I currently do not anticipate any new exhibits being brought into the system as a result of this file, but some of the documents are already exhibits and the index should indicate which are.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, behind tab 1 in this file is the statement you made in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, I'm going to look at page 11 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for you, Witness 29, if you turn to the second half of the documents behind tab 1, you'll see that there is an Albanian translation of your witness statement. And if you could turn, please, to the last two paragraphs on page 15, I'm going to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if the usher can find page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about the last two paragraphs on page 15, and the first two paragraphs on page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which for Your Honours are the last four paragraphs on page 11 from the words: "I heard shots being fired," down to the end of page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you aware that some of the text here might ask for private session? That was remained unnoticed during the first session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we look at page 11, fourth paragraph from the bottom, the third word from the end of that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That has been overlooked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In those four paragraphs, you set out the account that you've given us of how you say you sustained your injury. I just want to ask you one or two questions first of all. Is it right, as you say in the first of those four paragraphs, and in the first sentence of that paragraph, the first three words, that shots were being fired by other people during this incident, that there were generally shots being fired in the area where this incident took place. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it right, as well, that when you say you heard a shot at a time when Mr. Haradinaj was standing at your back with a pistol in his hand, that you didn't even realise at that point you'd been shot. Is that right as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in a that misstates his testimony. He didn't say Mr. Haradinaj was standing behind him. He was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a detail which would create no confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it right, Witness 29, that at the time when you say you were shot, you didn't realise that you had been shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that at that moment I heard somebody say, "Let's kill (redacted)," and Mr. Haradinaj said, "I'll kill him with my own hands." But because of the pain on my whole body, I did not realise that the bullet had hit me, at that moment I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to realise that it was a bullet shot that had hit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So were you still struggling with Mr. Haradinaj at a time when you realised it was a bullet shot, or was it after the struggle had come to an end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I realised when I saw the blood flowing, and then I saw the arm and I saw the bullet, the exit point of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Were you wearing your uniform? Did your uniform have arms at that point? Were you wearing sleeves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you appreciated that it was a bullet wound, were you still struggling with Mr. Haradinaj or was the struggle over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I realised exactly what had happened was when I went to that private home, when I saw my body that was covered in blood, that's where I realised a hundred per cent what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you didn't realise you had been shot until the incident was over and you'd left the scene. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. At the moment I received that wound, it was unbelievable to me that I had been shot; but when I left and went to this place we're talking about, I saw all my arm covered in blood. But I realised at the moment when I was hit, a little bit afterwards, when I saw the blood that I had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I put the question to you again. Was it during the struggle with Mr. Haradinaj that you realised you had been shot, or was it after that struggle was over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'm giving the same answer. At that moment, I realised I was wounded. Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer very precise is: "You said shortly after you were shot, you realised that you were shot." The question now is: "Had by then the struggle with Mr. Haradinaj already ended, or were you still struggling with him when you noticed that you must have been hit by a bullet?" That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The struggle was still going on. As soon as I heard the pistol shot, I realised that I had been hit. But I thought I would die from that wound. I never thought I would survive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were aware already of having been hit when you were still struggling with Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haradinaj was still over me when I saw the blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look at the last of the four paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's for us the bottom paragraph on page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For you, it is the second paragraph on page 16. If you just cast your eye over that. Do we understand your evidence correctly? You never saw Mr. Haradinaj discharge a fire-arm, but you concluded that it must have been him because he was standing right behind you with a pistol in his hand, and that is where the injury occurred. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when Mr. Haradinaj wounded me, nobody else was over me. So it was his pistol against my body and his pistol that wounded me. There's nothing else to be said. The truth is that Mr. Haradinaj wounded me, and nobody else was over me, except Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, that is a process which you've worked out from the position he was in. You never saw him shoot at you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I saw with my own eyes Mr. Haradinaj over me when he shot me. Nobody else could have hit me. Mr. Haradinaj had his pistol against my neck, the back of my neck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether your conclusion is right or wrong is another matter, but conclusions are here to be drawn by the Trial Chamber on the basis of the evidence. Simply: Did you see his finger pull the trigger? Did you see that with your eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw the moment he was over me, and he pulled the trigger in the direction of my neck. It was just destiny that saved me. Mr. Haradinaj pulled the trigger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From all your gestures, it seems that the weapon was not within the sight of your eyes. I'm not saying that you're wrong or you're right, but we just want to establish whether the weapon held, as you said by Mr. Haradinaj, was within your view or whether it was perhaps very close or just on your shoulder or you may have felt it. It could be anything, but whether you could see that weapon at that time. Don't worry about inferences. Don't worry about conclusions. If they have to be made, if they're logical, then, of course, it's up to the Chamber to make such conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. It was Mr. Haradinaj who was over me. It was Mr. Haradinaj's pistol, and I saw it with my own eyes when that pistol wounded me. I don't know how you as a Trial Chamber will interpret this. I have come here to describe the event as it was, as it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me put it clear to you. If I am here at this moment in this situation, I have difficulties on seeing what happens here. I can't see it with my eyes. That's the problem. That doesn't mean that it didn't happen as you said, but I can't see what is on the back of my shoulder. I may feel it, I may hear it. I may everything, but I can't see it. So now the question is -- and don't worry about what conclusions should be drawn or should not be drawn. The Chamber on the basis of all the evidence will make all the determinations it will have to make. But did you see the finger of Mr. Haradinaj pulling the trigger, or is it just that you knew that he was just behind you and that you were at that time shot where you could not imagine anyone else to do that than Mr. Haradinaj? That's the situation. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haradinaj wounded me. I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we've understood the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say in your witness statement - and this is the bottom of the last paragraph on page 11 - the bottom of your second paragraph on page 16, you say: "Because of the angle and direction, the bullet passed through my upper arm. I do not believe the shot could have been fired by anyone other than Ramush." Is this a proper summary of the evidence you are able to give? That's what you said in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty here is to explain the situation as it was. Mr. Haradinaj wounded me with his gun. I don't know how you interpret the sentence. The truth is that Mr. Haradinaj wounded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think the matter has been sufficiently explored.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me be clear, I want to take you through your evidence, please, from the moment you saw him draw his gun to the moment you left the scene. Now, you told us you saw him draw his gun, is that right, as he was approaching you? Is that correct, as he approached you and Idriz?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first moment Ramush was behind me before he hit Idriz Ukehaxhaj; then Ramush moved towards the car, overtook me on the right, and then went to Idriz --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and hit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Listen very carefully. You've told us when he hit Idriz, he had the gun in his hand. Is that right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pistol was in his right hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him take the pistol out in the first place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he drew the pistol, I could not see him because he was behind me. I only saw him when he overtook me, and he had the pistol in his hand and hit the person on both sides of his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's clear. So you saw him as he overtook you, and he already had the pistol in his hand. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have seen him when he drew the pistol. I don't know whether he drew the pistol out two metres or one metre behind me. I don't know. I just saw him when he overtook me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just listen to the question. When he overtook you, he already had the pistol in his hand. Is that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I can't say when exactly. But when he came where I could see him, he had the pistol in his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
