utterances.text: Witness 29, no one asked you. The simple question was: Did you see him draw his pistol? The answer clearly is no, because you said, "I could not see him when he drew the pistol." So Mr. Emmerson asked for the second or the third time, although it's perfectly clear to everyone that he had in the pistol in his hand when he overtook you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Witness 29, from the moment you first saw the pistol in Mr. Haradinaj's hand to the moment when he jumped on your back, did you see him shoot his pistol at any time, between the time when he -- you first saw it in his hand and the time when you say he jumped on your back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first thing that happened was that he hit Idriz, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Listen very carefully to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again the question: Mr. Haradinaj overtook you. Sometime later, as you said, he was standing behind you, and you're convinced that he fired a bullet into your arm. Did he fire his gun in between, or was that the first shot, the shot that hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were shots around; but whether it was Mr. Haradinaj's pistol or other guns, I couldn't identify them. But while he hit Idriz with both hands, there were shots around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer simply is: I don't know. It may have been that Mr. Haradinaj fired his gun before this bullet hit me. That's a simple answer. You don't have to explain it. Just focus on the question. Yes. It's quite clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Witness 29, apart from the time when you say he shot you in your arm, did he at any other time shoot at you during this incident or just the once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He shot at me only once when he wounded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you saw the gun in his hand. After this, you told us a few moments ago in your evidence - this is page 61, line 10 - you said: "After the incident calmed down, he still had his pistol in his hand," and you saw this, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, listen. I want to say something to make it clear. At the moment when someone shouted, "Let us kill (redacted)," and then Ramush Haradinaj said, "I will kill (redacted) with my own hand," from that moment, I saw him coming towards me with his pistol in his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, we'll return into private session for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, this document here records if you -- Witness 29 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Listen to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, behind tab 3, maybe with the usher's assistance. I'm going to show you now a witness, interview which you gave to the UNMIK police on the 9th of August, 2004. And if you could just look, first of all, immediately behind -- before the usher takes you to that passage, just at the very front page behind tab 3. Do you have tab 3 there? Do you see your signature there about halfway down the page on the, right-hand side, opposite your name. Do you see your signature, just where your right index finger is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you pass the bundle to me? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see your signature there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it in two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you turn over the page where there's some English writing, you see it at the bottom of the page as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, as will be clear, you've signed every page of this document, indicating at the end that you had had it read to you, fully understood it, and agreed with its contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, for Your Honours, I'm looking at page 85. That's the second page, and its number's at the bottom in pencil at questions 6 and question 8. And for the witness, the Albanian translation is just behind the green tab. Page 89 is question 6 and just over the page, page 90, is question 7. If you could direct the witness's attention to question 6 and question 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to read both questions and answers to you, Witness 29; both of them first, before I ask you to comment on them. Question 6: "Will you please tell us specifically about the nature of your complaint against Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, reading at a slower pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "A. On the 4th of July, 2004, [as read] during the war here in Kosovo, Ramush Haradinaj for no apparent reason shot me several times from behind with the use of his hand-gun with the intention to kill me. I survived said attempt on my life. I was only hit once on my right shoulder." Question 8: "Will you please narrate to us in detail how you managed to escape from that attempt on your life by Ramush Haradinaj?" Your answer: "Ramush Haradinaj, after firing several shots on me, he runs out of ammunition. At that instant, Ramush was then hesitant to get closer or attack me further as I faced him ready to defend myself, although I was badly injured. Sensing Ramush was really hesitant from making any further attack on me, I decided to run away and was able to escape." Now, Witness 29, when you were interviewed by the UNMIK police in August 2004, I suggest that you told them that Ramush Haradinaj shot you several times until he ran out of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shot at you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Shot at you several times until he ran out of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I give you my answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he fired several times and this is true, and others fired as well. I couldn't identify who it was that fired. The important thing here is that I was wounded by Mr. Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just look at your answer at page 93, line 4, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That might be difficult for the witness to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you read it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. We're not in the bundle anymore. I'm looking at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago in your evidence, Witness 29: "He shot at me once only when he wounded me." And then a little later on, when you were asked questions by the Judge, you made it clear that although you saw the gun in his hand, subsequently, there was never any further shot. I want to ask you why you told the UNMIK police in August of 2004 that he shot at you several times until he ran out of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj started to shoot at the first moment, and his munition didn't last 500 shots. At the moment he wounded me, I still heard shots. I couldn't say whether these shots were his or others, but I do say that he fired several times and that only one bullet hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So is it your evidence now that you saw him fire more than one shot, Witness 29?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even at the moment that he struck Ukehaxhaj, he still kept firing his weapon. He shot -- he struck him with his pistol and fired. The same happened with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say to you how many times he hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You just told us a few minutes ago that though those there were shots being fired, you don't think any one of them was shot by Mr. Haradinaj. He may have done; he may not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, please. At the moment when someone shouted, "Let's kill (redacted)," and he said, "I'll kill him with my own hand," he only hit me with one bullet. I cannot say that he -- I have 20 bullet wounds sustained on my body by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the point at least is clear. There is some inconsistency which is not fully explained at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you looked at your arm, did you see powder burns around the wound, Witness 29?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the powder burns afterwards when I went to get treatment. My jacket was pierced, and it was burnt a little bit. How can I explain? It was a little bigger than the actual bullet-hole. When the exit hole was almost the same as the one that was seen on the jacket in terms of size.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, you say you were shot effectively at point-blank range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about Mr. Haradinaj now?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say you were shot by Mr. Haradinaj at point-blank range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was wounded, he was very, very close. The pistol was behind my back and because I moved, the bullet hit me where it did; otherwise, I would have been hit on my neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I see. And you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it's lack of knowledge of language. "Point-blank range" exactly is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Immediately up against the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is that a touching the target or is could it be at a distance of two, three, four, five centimetres?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Point-blank range means so close to be in a few centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His pistol was on my back. It was next to me. It was not far. It was on my body. I could feel it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was asking some clarification from Mr. Emmerson what exactly he meant. Please listen to the next question, Witness 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Presumably, Witness 29, you would accept with all those armed KLA men in the area, if they wanted to kill you, they would have had no trouble doing it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did what they wanted to do. Apparently, they deemed it appropriate to leave it at that. There is no other explanation I can give.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I want to suggest to you, Witness 29, that although you were involved in a fight at Gllogjan that day, that you've told a number of deliberate lies about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Is there a question pending here or is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- my colleague just expounding on his own view of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm putting my case. It's a requirement of the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I would ask if this witness is being asked a question, he be asked a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm putting my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this is an objection and not a question, then it's denied. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I suggest, Witness 29, that it's not true that you saw or spoke to Ramush Haradinaj in Isniq on the 4th of July. If you listen carefully to the suggestions I'm putting to you, I'll ask you to respond to them at the end. I suggest that it's not true that you in Isniq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Irzniq not Isniq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's properly pronounced by Mr. Emmerson, but it is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you ask me about Isniq village, it is true that I did not speak to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put my question carefully. I am going to suggest to you that you did not see or speak to Ramush Haradinaj in Irzniq on the 4th of July, that you were never taken to Gllogjan at all within, that you drove there on your route to Pacaj, and that you were stopped and got into a dispute with the guards manning the check-point at Gllogjan. I suggest to you, you never went inside the KLA HQ, and you never spoke to Ramush Haradinaj inside the HQ, but that you got into an argument with the KLA guards about 50 metres from the HQ. You refused to obey their commands because you thought that as FARK soldiers you didn't have to take orders from them. A fight broke out. Shots were fired, and that it was at that point that Ramush Haradinaj ran up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, that's a very compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Well, it's put to the witness a different course of events, and I take it that Mr. Emmerson wants to know whether the witness agrees that that is what actually happened, rather than what he told us before. Mr. Kearney, I think Mr. Emmerson is under a duty under Rule, I think it's, 89(H), or something like that, to put to the witness -- let me just have a look -- but please proceed meanwhile. I'll have a look at the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I suggest further that he never drew his weapon, he never threatened to kill you, and he certainly never shot at you, although shots were being fired in the fracas that had taken place. That is the case I am suggesting to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I gave my answer or should I wait?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please give your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything I stated here is true. With respect to the questions or opinions of the Defence lawyer, it's as if I were going to tell him, We were in Amsterdam having a coffee. I cannot be here and not tell you the truth. I cannot say something which is not true. What he is saying, it's his business. I cannot say anything. The truth is what I already stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I was referring to Rule 90(H), where if counsel invites a witness to give evidence relevant for his case, then, of course, the case is what, in the view of the Defence, happened, that counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party in this respect. So therefore, that's what Mr. Emmerson did. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to turn to the more general questions that you have given evidence in relation to FARK, but to do it quickly because we are under time pressure, so if you can keep your answers as short as possible. First of all, I want to suggest to you on the day after this incident, on the 5th of July, Ramush Haradinaj had a meeting with Tahir Zemaj in Luke, just east of Decane, in which the incident that you had been involved with was the subject of discussion. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Zemaj met, but I don't know on what date, and I know that Mr. Haradinaj apologised to him. That's why they met, only for him to apologise; that is, I made a mistake. The situation got out of control. I couldn't control myself. This is more or less what he told Zemaj, at least as I heard it. I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You are aware, though, that the meeting took place, I suggest, in fact, it was the 5th of July, the day after the incident. And what Mr. Haradinaj told Mr. Zemaj, I suggest, and what Mr. Zemaj told you, is that Mr. Haradinaj had apologised for the behaviour of the guards, in the sense that the situation had got out of control. But that as far as he understood, you and your colleagues had begun the confrontation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were the ones who started the confrontation, why then did Mr. Haradinaj come to Mr. Zemaj to apologise? This shows that he understood that he was in error, and he came to apologise. At least this is what my commander told me, that Mr. Haradinaj accepted the mistake, apologised: This is not going to happen anymore. I couldn't control the situation -- contain myself. The situation got out of control. It was very wrong. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, you know full well that Ramush Haradinaj never said to Tahir Zemaj that he could not control himself because you discussed this with Tahir Zemaj, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present at that meeting between Mr. Zemaj and Mr. Haradinaj, but I can only relay the words that my commander told me, that Mr. Haradinaj apologised, the situation got out of control, I made a mistake, and I'm not going to repeat the mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me come to one or two other general questions about the evidence you've given in relation to the relationship between FARK and the KLA. And I want to suggest to you as a general proposition that there were some initial problems of integration between the newly arrived forces and the existing KLA; that those problems lasted no more than two weeks; and that by the 10th of July, as our regards show, the forces that Tahir Zemaj had brought into the Dukagjini region had been fully integrated within the KLA, under the command of Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? The fact is that Mr. Haradinaj was a self-proclaimed commander. I don't know who had appointed him in that position. In the case of Mr. Zemaj, there was another structure. Someone had appointed him commander. And, of course, Mr. Haradinaj had to welcome Mr. Zemaj because, in fact, Mr. Zemaj was the general, overall commander for the entire Dukagjin Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what Mr. Zemaj thought because he was operating under instructions from Ahmet Krasniqi. Is that right? He thought he was the overall commander of the Dukagjini Zone and was marching into it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If any Albanian, any member of the KLA, wanted to call themselves as a soldier, fighting for the future of Kosova, they had to obey the orders of the prime minister and of the president. Whoever disobeyed such orders, let them have their own responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 29, there were two separate structures giving orders during the period immediately after FARK came into Kosovo, weren't there? There was Tahir Zemaj taking orders from Ahmet Krasniqi; and then there was an existing structure within Kosovo which had no connection to Ahmet Krasniqi or the Bukoshi government. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we entered Kosova, some agreements were already in place. I wasn't part of such agreement, but I know that there was an agreement. We didn't go there just because we wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I want to -- you've mentioned disagreements that took place in the Jasic area. Although, you told us you weren't there at the meeting, you've given us an account of what you were told took place, with threats being made against FARK soldiers and so forth. Is it really the position that you don't know what the nature of the disagreement was? Do you really not know what they were disagreeing about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement that I mentioned and that was referred to at the time was that the KLA will welcome the FARK, will cooperate with it, and will be placed under its supervision; that is, under the supervision of the FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that was the understanding that Tahir Zemaj had, I suggest. When you first arrived, is it not correct that you were -- the officers were given a feast. There was a large meal laid on for them by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Jasic village, the entire population of the village, that welcomed us, and I can say that they welcomed us very warmly. I'm talking about the people's reception, not about the KLA. I explained to you how the KLA and Ramush Haradinaj received us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were then a series of meetings; some at Junik and some at Jasic. And if you are telling us the truth that you were being provided with information from Tahir Zemaj, you will know, I suggest, that the disagreement was because the KLA commanders wanted the trained officers of the FARK to be distributed to reinforce defences in different parts of the Dukagjin Zone; whereas, Tahir Zemaj had instructions from Ahmet Krasniqi to keep the FARK forces as one unit. You knew, didn't you, that that was the nature of the disagreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke only about Jasic reception. In Junik and other places, I was in Isniq village, trying to find some places to accommodate our forces in order to escape the fratricide with Mr. Haradinaj. From what I know, because I wasn't part of the agreement, I cannot speak here for things which is not part of my knowledge is that Mr. Tahir Zemaj should be the overall commander for the 3rd operational zone of Dukagjin. Whereas Ramush Haradinaj who was a commander before we entered Kosova would be incorporated into the force -- into the FARK, that was it. But Mr. Haradinaj acted in opposition to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson before you continue you earlier said if you are providing us with the truth about information, et cetera, you will know, that ignores that the information might not be correct that has been provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You ignored that, and that should be refrained from. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I suggest that after the week or so that you spent in the Jasic area or that the FARK forces spent in the Jasic area, the difficulties were resolved to the extent that the FARK forces were able to march up to Isniq, going through Gllogjan. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, they had some other meetings but I wasn't present at them. And from what I learned later from the commander, during that period they had threatened us again and threatened us to go back to the territory of Albania. But the order was given to us to enter Kosova; then the problem was resolved through understanding that we leave Jasic, an understanding between our superior officers to avoid any bloodshed. But on the way, Mr. Haradinaj's forces attempted to prevent us, but Mr. Krasniqi had ordered us to continue our march. So the order was given to us to go to Isniq at all costs, irrespective of any threats, any circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The KLA soldiers under the command of Ramush Haradinaj fought side by side with FARK soldiers at the battle of Loxha on the 6th of July just two days after the incident you've described, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battle was waged at Loxha. The army from there was led by Tahir Zemaj. There were also members of the KLA who were inhabitants of Loxhe village but everything was led by Colonel Zemaj, at least this is what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The barracks at Prapaqan, they were provided by Ramush Haradinaj, they were KLA barracks in which Rrustem Teta had been training KLA soldiers and they were handed over to Tahir Zemaj, weren't they, on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went to Prapaqan, there was no kind of investment made there. There were no soldiers being trained. We transformed the school into barracks. That place needed some investment, you know, beds to be put in there, and everything was done by Commander Tahir Zemaj. Later on, some from Mr. Ramush Haradinaj came there and we welcomed them. The commander welcomed them to train them, but this was after we settled there in the school. It's not what you told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just have a look behind tab 4, would you were briefly, please, Witness 29. Behind tab 4 in the bundle, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could help.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll just go through these very briefly with you if I could. Behind tab 4(A), first of all, and there's a translation on the third and fourth pages. That's an order signed by Ramush Haradinaj deploying KLA soldiers to the Prapaqan barracks on the 8th of July. Do you accept that there were KLA soldiers at Prapaqan barracks from the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I said that we were the first there, and later about 50 soldiers from Mr. Haradinaj came there. They had a commander who was from Gjakove, if I'm not mistaken, but I'm not sure. But as I said, we were the first there. They came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Lets just be clear. You say in your witness statement that it was the 8th of July that you went there. There were KLA soldiers there with you at that time, weren't there, in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went there, I said Mr. Tahir Zemaj, the commander, created that place. I cannot say things here that are untrue. He paid for some of the things that were needed there. These were not procedures that I was involved in. Mr. Tahir Zemaj dealt with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you just look at tab 5(B) for a moment, that is a request by Tahir Zemaj addressed to the Dukagjin Plain Operative Staff, of the 10th of July, requesting the formation of three brigades of his officers. If you follow over, there's 4 (B), 5 (A), and 35 (B), you can see Ramush Haradinaj authorising the requests and establishing the brigades on the 12th of July. So by the 10th of July, if you can see the request from Tahir Zemaj, he's referring to an agreement from the 10th of July requesting and proposing that the officers listed below be appointed to certain functions. So by the 10th of July, would you accept that Tahir Zemaj was fully absorbed within the Dukagjin Plain Operative Staff, under the command of Ramush Haradinaj, just two weeks or so after FARK arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me questions I have no competence over. I cannot speak here about things I do not know. The thing I am saying here is when we first went there, there was no soldier of Mr. Haradinaj there. I was a simple soldier. I had senior officers who dealt with these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally, this: I suggest as you lied about the incident at Gllogjan, Witness 29, you deliberately tried to persuade the Trial Chamber falsely, and knowing it was false, that during this period of time FARK were under threat from KLA, when in fact there were a number of organisational difficulties that were resolved in a period of two weeks. That is my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Objection to the phrase "at that time." It's vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, within the two weeks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's clear everything was rotating around let's say, early July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The two weeks between the 24th of June when they entered and the 10th of July when it is perfectly plain that they were fully integrated. That's the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, Witness 29, Mr. Emmerson puts to you that there were no threats by the KLA or that FARK was under threat of the KLA; and, in fact, there were a number of organisatorial [sic] difficulties which were resolved in two weeks. That is what he puts to you. Would you agree with that, or would you say that's not true, what Mr. Emmerson puts to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My duty here is to tell the truth. Whatever the learned Defence lawyer says here, it's his duty. He has to do his duty. What I'm saying here is the complete opposite of what the lawyer just stated here, and those are my experiences that I lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, was that your last question? Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Quite briefly, in order to save as much time as I can, I make the exact same two suggestions to the witness that were previously made by Mr. Emmerson with regard to the issue concerning FARK, as well as the issue concerning what happened during July 4th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're putting exactly the same to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm putting exactly the same, and I'm moving on from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it what the answers given to Mr. Emmerson are answers in the case against all accused, so therefore there's no need to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excellent. I won't concern myself with that anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness 29, simply put, you are much more than a simple soldier. As a matter of fact, you were tasked specifically by your superiors to go into the region, as you told us, between January and the time you finally entered in June to make a determination of how the population was to defend themselves and "if it was a situation where we could fight." Is that correct? That's what you've told us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But I said I was not a senior officer; because had I been a senior officer, that would have meant that I finished some kind of military academy or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. You've also told us that during -- during the period of time that you were engaged in your reconnaissance missions to make a determination whether or not the group you were assigned to that could come in and fight, the movements of the population became more difficult, and that would be after March 24th. I would like for you to comment on what you meant by the movements of the population became more difficult. Is that as a result of the fact that you saw yourself that wide-scale numbers of the population were, in fact, fleeing from various areas because of the Serb bombing, shelling, or other kinds of assaults?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The movement of the population became even more difficult after the 24th of March because the KLA emerged at that time and the enemy forces wanted to eliminate the KLA. So in some situations the people living in the villages didn't want to get caught up in confrontation. This was why the population had -- it was difficult for the population to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say the population didn't want to get caught up in the confrontation, these were things you saw. You actually saw villages of people trying to escape the area because of what was happening due to the Serb assaults; correct? This was a kind of information that you were reporting back to your superiors in Albania when you would go back from one of your ten trips; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went back, I reported on the basis of the assessments that I had made, and it may be that my assessments were not a hundred per cent accurate. But from what I saw, the people wanted to live, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Being, if it is fair to say, the eyes and ears of Tahir Zemaj, when you were going into the field on these trips, you mentioned, among other things, that you were trying to make an assessment of the preparation by self-defence by the "peasants," were your words. And what I would like to understand, when you were trying to make that determination, was that one of the things that occurred when you were going from village to village, you were trying to figure out how many of the peasants were involved in trying to defend their own villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain as correctly as possible. These were visits that I was assigned with by Mr. Sali Ceku and Commander Zemaj; initially by Mr. Ceku. However, my assessments were not, I think, a hundred per cent accurate possibly, because I could not be in the position to do a full assessment. But the people wanted to stay and defend their villages. They could not just stay there and be attacked. They had to take up arms and defend their own villages. It was not possible for the KLA to defend everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- with only a couple of guns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you misrepresented the evidence of the witness in relation to the peasants. I checked it. He didn't say he was trying to an assessment of the preparation of self-defence by the peasants, but he said what he observed; that is, that sometimes, it was just self-defence by peasants.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I did not mean to misrepresent it, and as I see it, it says: "Only some preparations for self-defence by the peasants were under way." I believe that's his exact language on page 13, line 22. But I wasn't trying to misrepresent anything. The point that I was driving at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The point I was driving at is as follows, and I will ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which is: During the period of time you were trying to make an assessment of what was going on on the ground, one of the things you were making an assessment about was some of the preparations for self-defence by the peasants that were underway; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The peasants, or the villagers, wanted to get guns as soon as possible. They wanted to defend themselves. They couldn't have military structures. The population was interested in self-defence, to get some guns and be able to defend themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. When you visited the villages that you mentioned to us, those being: Smolice, Ponoshec, Racaj, Junik, Herec, Gramaqel, Irzniq, and Luka, did you have a chance to make a determination who was the village commander of each of those villages while you were on your trips making assessments for your superiors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were periods when I went to Kosovo, and there were no village commanders. I went to Kosovo even before the 24th of March when the KLA had not emerged yet; while after the 24th every village, although every village, although I can't say each and every village, it's better to say some of the villages had begun to organise themselves in the meaning that they had assigned a certain commander for the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as you sit here today, with regard to the villages that you mentioned in your direct testimony and I just asked you about, who the village commanders were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any minutes here to tell me who was the commander for each village. I've written down some names when I visited the villages in the commune of Decane; however, when I talked to some of the villagers and people, representatives in Decane, they told me that Mr. Haradinaj was in command in that area. I was just a simple soldier then. Other people evaluated the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is with regard, once again, to the village commander. For example, did you know who was the village commander for the village of Smolice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know even today who the commander in Smolice was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Ponoshec?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. At that time, I was just trying to assess the situation. I was not writing down all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just tell us if you know it. I take it that, Mr. Guy-Smith, you would like to go through all of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I would like to do them as quickly as possible, and I can repeat them. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Racaj. Do you know who the commander there was? If you don't know just tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Junik, same question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Junik was divided into some parts, but I don't think they had a commander. Somebody came with us, and he was assigned a commander; while in the area of Reka e Keqe, Salih Veseli was a commander there. Although, I am not very sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Gramaqel, do you know the name of a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Irzniq, I take it that you mentioned the name of the commander there already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the early period. It was very early. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rrustem Teta, people said that he was commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know an individual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm looking at the clock, and I don't know what you had in mind. I asked earlier whether the Defence considered that they could finish if we would have half an hour in addition, and then I got the message that most likely they would be able to do so. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey. Would you need any additional time for re-examination, Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, five minutes are granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know an individual by the name of Sami Tahiri from the village of Beleg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sami Tahiri, he lives in Switzerland, and he was a prisoner after the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Zenon Idrizi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you involved in an assault on Baballoq with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was to some extent I would say, but not directly involved because duties were assigned to us, as always; and in the assault of Baballoq that you are asking me, there were three other persons. I wasn't directly involved in that assault. I had another task assigned, as the case was in other instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Due to the time constraints that exist, I'm going to ask you a question concerning what you've told us here today, which is that you claimed in your testimony that when you were on your way to the headquarters at Gllogjan, that you were driven between two cars and when you arrived that one of the cars, being driven by Togeri, parked behind you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left for Gllogjan, Daut was before we behind. When we arrived in Gllogjan, Togeri was parked behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall making a statement in 2006?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm referring the Court and counsel to paragraph 13 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is a statement you correct your previous statement, and you say the following: "At page 9 of my statement, where I stated Idriz parked his car about 50 metres from the entrance to the yard of the Gllogjan, the KLA headquarters, I can clarify that Daut parked his car in front of mine, but I did not see where Togeri went in his car." When you made that correction to your statement, you were telling the truth then, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement - and it is very clear to me how it happened - Daut parked the car in front of us; Toger behind us. I didn't say where Togeri went. We parked in the middle about 50 metres far from him, and there was nothing left for us to do. We were like in a sandwich position. What could we do? We had gone there to talk. We hadn't gone there to fight. I had met Mr. Haradinaj half an hour before, so I went there without any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And a final question: I suggest to you that at the store area, you never had any contact with Toger whatsoever, and he never shot any gun up in the air or threatened you in any fashion whatsoever. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you give me the opportunity to tell the truth, I will say the truth. How you put it, it's your business. The truth is this, and if you want me I will repeat it. Toger threatened us and brought out his weapon and even threatened us with his weapon and even fired up in the air with his weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that that -- when he did that, according to your testimony, is what he did he pulled his weapon out and immediately fired it into the air. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After them insisting on us getting into their car and taking us to where they wanted, and after us then agreed, because what could we do? I could go to Mr. Haradinaj, for me it would have been a pleasure having met him half an hour ago. But I just said, I don't want to come with your car. That was a solution we agreed on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Toger pulled out his pistol --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether he pulled out his weapon and immediately fired this, whether that is your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Toger pulled out his weapon and told us that, "You have to come with us in our car," and that he fired in the air. I may not tell you exactly how many times he did, but for sure five times, even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before he -- before you saw him do that, fire his weapon in the air five times, did you watch him load his weapon? Did he take his pistol out and load it and then fire it in the air?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, that misstates his answer that he fired it five times in the air.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was two, three metres away from me. I could see each and every movement of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't mean to misrepresent his testimony with regard to how many times he fired in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question is this: You saw him pull out his pistol; and before he fired it into the air, did you see him load his pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot load the weapon when you pull it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 29, quite clear. When he drew his weapon, before he fired, did you see him loading his weapon or, that's the opposite, was it already loaded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He kept the pistol all the time in his hand, then he loaded it, and then immediately fired in the air five or six times. This is what I saw and this is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recall when you made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I gave you five minutes. You have now seven and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: May I ask one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall when you told UNMIK in your statement in 2004 what occurred regarding this incident, which is question 7, the following: "Lieutenant Idriz Balaj immediately drew his hand-gun, loaded it, and fired about four shots in the air."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are asking me another question, I will give you an answer, but I already answered your question. He fired five or six times. He loaded it and fired in the air to force us to get into his car. That is the long and the short of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I asked for one more question; I got one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, you asked for one more question as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 29, you were asked many questions about exactly what happened during the period when you were beaten and when you were shot. I want to ask you simply: Could you please tell us what your physical and mental state was during that time-period when you were being beaten and being shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/29 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can understand what my mental state would be. When somebody beats you in that fashion, when someone wounds you for no reason at all, you can imagine what it is like, in a very bad state indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honours has it in mind to ask the witness to produce the notes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I wonder if you would make an order that the notebook itself and all copies of the notebook should remain with the Tribunal; in other words, any copies that the witness may have of the notebook in his possession should be handed to the Prosecution and kept for safe-keeping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The notebook or notes? Because the notebook was returned to the Prosecution. Witness 29, would you mind to leave the notebook for the time being, the original, in the hands of the Prosecution and then perhaps copies could be made for yourself, so that you, if you want to, consult what was in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For reasons, that might be best be dealt with without the witness's headphones. I'm anxious that he should not take with him any copies of the content of the notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Kearney, any problems with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, I'm going to suggest that perhaps the Trial Chambers might consider sending someone from VWS to go with the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- to get the notes and bring them back to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And up to that moment, to keep the original. Has any copy been made and provided to you, Witness 29, or have you made any copies yourself of the notebook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't make any copies because I brought it here to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll keep the notebook for the time being. That does not mean you will not receive a copy of the original back perhaps at a later stage, but for the time being we would like to keep it in the Tribunal. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever you deem appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But if you either keep a copy or give me the original or the other way around, as you think it's best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll receive that at a later stage, not immediately. Is that understood? Then I would like to instruct you, since you said you are willing to provide all the notes you still have, to accept to be accompanied by someone of the Victims and Witnesses Section to accompany you to any place where you keep one of these notes, and to provide them to the person that accompanies you, or someone assigned by the Victims and Witnesses Section, because I do not know exactly where the limits of their competence is. They might find someone to secure that. So you are now under an order to provide all these notes. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is also my pleasure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's good to hear; then I'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague. Whether it will be necessary at any later stage to ask you to come back, we do not know yet. It might be that there's no need for that. It might be otherwise. We do not know, but you'll be informed about it if that's the case. Yes, Mr. Emmerson, can the witness be excused already?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I was just going to say, to save time, I'll deal with the exhibits of documents that were dealt with in cross-examination first thing, if I may, when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's best. Witness, thank you very much. I wish you a safe trip home again. Yes, you are excused. Yes. We'll deal with all the administrative matters at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there something you need to bring to my attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just that we need to read the 92 ter summary into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do that at a later time when we have time. Thank you to all the interpreters and the technicians and the usher and all others who were quite flexible to make it possible for us to finalise the information of Witness 29. We adjourn until the 7th of May, quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.29 p.m.,
